course.title: Playwright — Complete Deep Testing Course
course.description: A Playwright-specific, beginner-to-advanced automation course with detailed concepts, practical browser testing, dedicated tasks, debugging, CI integration and a complete learning-platform capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn the testing tool properly; no fixed cross-tool template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Handle synchronization and test data correctly.
Debug failures and integrate tests into CI.
Build a complete production-style E2E test suite.

modules.title: Playwright Foundations
modules.description: Browser contexts, pages, tests, locators and cross-browser automation.

lessons.title: Playwright Foundations
lessons.description: Browser contexts, pages, tests, locators and cross-browser automation.
learningObjectives: Apply it to a realistic web-testing workflow.

notes.text: Browser contexts, pages, tests, locators and cross-browser automation.

Learn playwright foundations by understanding what the browser automation layer is doing, how the test controls the application, how synchronization works, and how to verify the result without creating fragile tests.

Playwright Foundations is important for building confidence in a real web application. Good automated tests reproduce meaningful user behavior while remaining isolated, deterministic, readable and maintainable.

notes.caption: Add a browser-testing diagram or screenshot-style visual explaining Playwright Foundations.

items: Test behavior and outcomes, not implementation details unnecessarily.
Use stable selectors and deterministic data.

notes.code:
Scenario: Create the first Playwright test.

Automation flow: arrange data -> navigate -> interact -> wait for state -> assert -> capture evidence -> cleanup.

items: Define the user journey or behavior.
Wait for the application state, not an arbitrary delay.
Adding fixed sleeps instead of condition-based waits.
Sharing mutable test data between tests.
Testing implementation details instead of user behavior.
Making one huge E2E test instead of focused journeys.
Use API setup when it makes tests faster and cleaner.
I can explain Playwright Foundations in my own words.
I can automate a small browser workflow.
I can choose a stable locator.
I can synchronize without arbitrary sleeps.
I can diagnose a failing test.

practicals.title: Guided Practical — Playwright Foundations
practicals.objective: Apply Playwright Foundations to a realistic learning-platform test scenario.
steps: Run the test repeatedly to check stability.
Capture debugging evidence if it fails.
practicals.starterCode:
# Playwright — Playwright Foundations
# Scenario: Create the first Playwright test.
practicals.expectedOutput: A stable automated test demonstrating Playwright Foundations.

tasks.title: Dedicated Task — Playwright Foundations
requirements: Use stable locators and deterministic state.
Document how to run and debug the test.
acceptanceCriteria: No unnecessary fixed waits are used.
Test data is isolated or safely managed.

quiz.question: What is the main focus of Playwright Foundations?
quiz.answer: Reliable browser/test automation using Playwright
quiz.explanation: The lesson focuses on applying Playwright Foundations to real web testing.

quiz.question: Which is generally better than a fixed sleep in browser automation?
options: Waiting for a meaningful application state
quiz.answer: Waiting for a meaningful application state
quiz.explanation: State-based synchronization is usually faster and more reliable than arbitrary delays.

summary: Learn to maintain and debug the test.
